title: A fixed 500 m carbon transfer ratio permits the ALOHA oxygen loss in a particle-mixture box
abstract: We test whether a carbon transfer ratio can exclude changed particle breakdown depth as a cause of ALOHA oxygen loss. For nonnegative mixtures of power laws, we prove sharp bounds on the carbon fraction lost between 300 and 700 m at fixed 500 m / 150 m flux. At transfer 0.20 the fraction can range from nearly zero to 0.26835. A single exponent gives the upper bound. A finite early mixture of exponents 0.1 and 5 and a later mixture keep transfer at 0.20. With the measured 1989-2024 HOT export history, this family can supply the published 3.32 mol O2/m2 density-corrected loss at a 30-year box renewal time. It needs at least 163 years to supply the full 4.82 mol/m2 loss. At fixed late transfer 0.20 and no renewal, explaining the residual requires an early layer fraction no larger than 0.12625. These are conditional capacity tests, not observed particle changes. The assumed broad early particle mixture, one-box transport, point targets and sparse trap sampling limit inference. Paired 300 m and 700 m flux measurements can test the alternative; a single transfer depth cannot.
